notes: Actual results for the fiscal year ended September 30, 2024, as the city reported them to the Census Bureau's Annual Survey of State and Local Government Finances. Not a budget.

The District runs its own public schools, so school spending is included and left out of the services and overhead shares. It also provides services states provide elsewhere, such as Medicaid and the state university.
Covers every fund, including water, sewer, electric and other utilities. Debt service counts interest and principal repaid; borrowing and transfers between funds are left out.
The city borrowed $2,246,057,000 during the year, which is not counted as revenue but helps explain spending above revenue.
Payments to other governments ($957,774,000) are left out, because the government receiving them reports that spending.
Courts, legal services, public buildings, housing and community development count as overhead.
Debt is long-term debt outstanding plus short-term debt at year end.

Political money counts contributions from businesses, unions and PACs to candidates for mayor, council and attorney general, reported to the Office of Campaign Finance since 2023. Candidates in the Fair Elections public financing program may not accept business or PAC money. Individuals, candidates' own money, in-kind gifts, party committees, and committees for the shadow congressional seats and the State Board of Education are not counted.
Transparency practices have not been checked yet, so they are not scored.

Cameras: 104 license-plate cameras are mapped inside City of Washington's borders in OpenStreetMap (89 made by Flock Safety), not counting cameras tagged as run by stores, malls, schools or state and regional agencies. Flock cameras count as a red flag whoever runs them. Other brands count only when the government is the recorded operator, since many have no operator recorded.

Red flags: surveillance programs come from the EFF Atlas of Surveillance, a public database of news reports and public records, searched on 2026-10-20. A town or county with none listed may still have programs nobody has reported. Data center deals and corporate tax breaks have not been checked for District of Columbia yet. Most records carry no dollar amount, so each documented program costs a quarter of the red-flag points instead of being counted as spending.

redFlags.label: Flock camera network
redFlags.detail: 89 Flock Safety license-plate cameras are mapped inside City of Washington's borders in OpenStreetMap. Flock cameras photograph every passing car and feed a search network shared with police agencies across the country. Who runs each camera is not recorded; cameras tagged as run by stores, malls, schools or state and regional agencies are not counted.
